notes: Delta design: run each query with and without the skill loaded. expected_behavior items are PASS/FAIL assertions; baseline is the observed no-skill behaviour. Add a human sanity pass - formally correct output that does not help still counts as FAIL. Record tokens and wall time per run alongside pass/fail. Activation is measured once for the whole family in evals/activation.json.

evals.query: write acceptance criteria for an RPN calculator
expected_behavior: produces numbered R<n> requirements, one testable statement each
names an observable outcome per requirement (exception type, return value)
lists what the task did not say as Q<n> instead of guessing
contains no module layout, class names or algorithms
evals.baseline: writes a prose paragraph mixing requirements with implementation hints, no numbering

evals.query: F-003 says 1 0 / raises ZeroDivisionError and no requirement covers it
expected_behavior: adds one new requirement for the division-by-zero contract
leaves every existing R<n> number untouched
rewrites the F-003 line with resolved true and a resolution naming the new requirement
evals.baseline: renumbers the requirement list, or tries to fix the code itself

evals.query: this requirement says the parser should handle errors gracefully
expected_behavior: flags it as untestable - no observable outcome
rewrites it naming the exception type and message shape

evals.query: while you are at it, sketch the module layout too
expected_behavior: declines - module layout belongs to the design phase
evals.baseline: produces a module layout and file structure
